name: Deep Bore Elevator
description: Industrial cargo elevators that descend into the Underworld through vertical shafts bored into the bedrock. The official ones are maintained by Ferrogate and reach the first three Underworld levels. Unofficial shafts — hand-cut, jury-rigged, dangerously maintained — go deeper. The descent is slow, dark, and accompanied by the sound of water dripping and metal groaning. The temperature drops as you descend. By Level 3, your breath is visible. Below that, the elevators aren't elevators anymore — they're cages on cables, and the cables are old.
propulsion: Electric cable winch (official), manual hand-crank or gravity-assisted (unofficial)
capacity: 8 persons or 2,000 kg (official), less for unofficial shafts
cost: Φ5 per descent (official). Unofficial operators charge Φ20-50 and don't guarantee the return trip.
common_usage: Underworld access, deep mining logistics, exploration, descent into the unknown.
story_hooks: An unofficial shaft's cable snaps and the cage falls — but it doesn't hit bottom. It keeps falling far longer than geology allows.
A Deep Bore Elevator that was sealed ten years ago starts cycling on its own, going down and coming back up at regular intervals
